# Design Backlog — the Topic Ledger

Every idea gets a row the moment it's uttered. Statuses:
`💡 candidate` (mentioned, not designed) → `📐 designed` (has a home in a design doc or
archive section) → `🔬 researched` (coverage-matrix row ✅ in `research/README.md`) →
`📜 RFC` (spec'd/implementing) → `⛔ rejected` (with reason, kept for the record).

Rules: **an idea missing from this ledger is a process bug** · **do NOT RFC from a
candidate row** (and per `rfc/0000-rfc-process.md`, not from any row until the
exploration gate opens). Honesty note: everything marked 🔬 below rests on the archive's
**desk research** — provenance effectively `[P]` until Phase-0 hands-on work upgrades it
(`archive/brief-v2/research/research_limitations.md` is the package's own accounting).

Archive homes are cited as `arch/NN §…` = `archive/brief-v2/NN_….md`.

| D1802 📊 | **THE RATING DEFECT IS ONE SHAPE, NOT THREE — AND THE PRIMARY KEY WAS NEVER THE MISTAKE.** [[D1516]] read `rated_games.run_id PRIMARY KEY` plus two bot-presupposing `NOT NULL` columns as three problems to widen. The draft found the actual cause: **`rated_games.result` is `win|loss|draw`, a value defined *relative to a learner*** (`outcome.ts:12` computes it against `data.start.side`). **A value relative to one participant cannot be shared by two**, so the primary key is not an oversight — it is the correct key for the value the column holds. **Re-orienting the declared result to colour** is the single change that makes the row a fact about the **game**, with each side's score a projection — *and that is exactly what a crosstable reads*. `rated_games` becomes `games` + `game_sides`, with `rating_before`/`rd_before`/`volatility_before` written **at admission** so a two-learner update **commutes**. The elegance is the argument: one re-orientation buys the native match and the tournament together | 📊 measured 2026-08-26 — `rfc/native-ratings.md`, `1cdedae7` |
| D1803 📊 | **THREE CLAIMS I LANDED IN [[D1529]] DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND ONE WAS STALE BY ELEVEN MIGRATIONS.** **(1)** `public_tokens.scope` admits **two** values at HEAD, not one — I quoted **migration 13**'s DDL; **migration 14 rebuilt the table** and the live `CHECK` is `('story_read','session_join')`, verified. Reading a migration's DDL instead of the live schema is a distinct failure from the census-scope defect in [[D1525]]: there the scope was too narrow; here the **snapshot was too old** | 📊 corrected 2026-08-26 — verify against the live schema, not the migration that created it |

Add mixed-producer positives and both false-advertisement negatives before either RFC is amended | 🐞 open 2026-08-26 — shared F1/provider contract blocker for [[D963]] and [[D1654]]; research repair in progress |

Close [[D963]] by deriving descriptive geometry from one exact declared position/pawn authority and adding a node-free live Syzygy position receipt (request FEN + source/result identity); the outcome event uses literal live-or-recorded `anyOf`, refuses cross-position joins, and keeps unavailable distinct from refuted. The generic live receipt belongs in the shared provider-exchange layer so Review and endgame modules do not create private Syzygy adapters | 🐞 open 2026-08-26 — research/contract closure in progress; blocks only `semantic-collectors` promotion-race ids 13/14 and shared live Syzygy consumption |

## Breadth-first product surfaces (owner-ratified 2026-08-11)

| D969 🐞 | **Bot-policy Stage A now has one measured production candidate, but the accepted RFC has not declared it.** One shared `MultiPV=N searchmoves` request is the only common scale; node 25k/50k is refused on completeness and depth 12 on latency. The exact 279-position / 837-cell R11 population was repriced at depth 8 and 10. Both pass the original guard gate and retain pawn ×4 while forcing/quiet ×3 fail. The typed rerun abstains on 11 mixed mate/cp positions (33 cells) rather than converting mate to fake cp; over the remaining 804 cells depth 8 removes 100% measured severe mass with 1.36 cp strengthening and 100.21% human-match retention, and pawn ×4 moves +12.28 pp with 98.79% retention. Depth 10 changes no gate verdict and carries a 729 ms cold tail; depth 8 stays below 500 ms. | 🐞 research complete 2026-08-23 — RFC amendment must pin depth 8, its multi-call budget and mixed-domain abstention, then bind them into the guarded/pawn-heavy profile digests before registration; no further empirical arm is required |
| D970 🔬 | **Bot-policy was accepted while its concrete Human-baseline roster is still an open question.** The D333 synthesis now gives one non-post-hoc 1.0 answer: expose the pre-registered bands `[1000,1400,1800,2200]`; all adjacent score intervals are disjoint, while 100-point steps are below learner-session resolution and the measured 2000→2400 increment crosses parity. They are human-policy bands, not Elo labels, and they attenuate at ≤10 pieces. Use band-specific model-layer identities; guarded/pawn-heavy variants remain behind D969 and per-digest calibration. | 🔬 researched 2026-08-23 — `design/research/maia-production-band-roster.md`; awaiting owner/RFC amendment before production declarations |
| D971 🐞 | **Intent-presets specifies five module lists but not the corresponding nine-field `AssistanceConfig` projections, and it describes `configClamp` as “the same ceilings” without a literal seven-context table.** Compiler rule 4 says output starts from “the preset's config projection,” yet no such values exist; only the match clamp and board-lighting invariant are concrete. Guessing whether Guided enables markers, whether Analysis enables human/corpus/evidence lighting, or what Stream/Academy clamp would recreate the raw-switch UX behind an untested preset label. Amend the accepted RFC with exact preset config rows, exact per-context clamp rows, and 5×7 expected-output fixtures. The closed ids, module sets, context module ceilings and derivation may land independently. | 🐞 open — blocks `compileAssistance` config output, preset pill/footer truth, and intent-presets A1/A4/A7/A10; RFC amendment/re-review required |
| D972 ✅ | **The shared ledger assigned both D967 and D968 twice.** Each id named one learner-modules blocker and one learner-rating follow-up, so `[[D967]]`/`[[D968]]` references were ambiguous and a closeout could flip the wrong obligation. The learner-module blockers retain D967/D968; the rating rows and every live-tier reference move atomically to D980/D981. | ✅ closed 2026-08-22 by the work-index implementation checkpoint |
| D973 ✅ | **`longitudinal-store.md` is registered `accepted` while all three of its Open questions still say “resolve before implementation”; the status history also says they remain unresolved.** The choices affect the v1 ingest set, whether an unmeasured bulk-import cost is accepted, and who owns every future derivation-revision bump. Implementing migration 26 or the derivation before those clauses are reconciled would turn an ambiguous acceptance into product policy. The 2026-08-24 amendment returns the RFC/register to draft and records all three answers: shapes excluded from rev 1, bulk projection backgrounded with durable progress, and the changing RFC owns the rev/rebuild discharge. | ✅ closed 2026-08-24 — lifecycle contradiction removed; amended contract awaits re-review |
| D974 ✅ | **The `/capabilities` response fixture pinned the pre-Wave-C evidence-manifest counts (25/146/182/40) after the compiled manifest reached 34 producers, 184 projections, 207 bindings and 65 semantic events.** CI therefore failed while the runtime response was internally current. The fixture now follows the compiled manifest's verified counts; this is a test reconciliation only, not a capability expansion. | ✅ closed 2026-08-22 in the learner-rating service checkpoint |
| D977 ⚖️ | **OWNER CORRECTION 2026-08-22 (theming draft): no license ceremony on color palettes, no version machinery on the theme preference** — verbatim: *"why would you do versioned catalogues or MIT attribution to a collection of color codes from common themes?"* Two fixes ruled: (1) a palette of hex values is not copyrightable subject matter — the license-verification acceptance criterion applies to **piece-set SVG artwork only** (genuinely mixed licenses in lila's catalog); palettes keep at most a courtesy source comment, never a criterion. (2) The theme preference follows the owner's own reference pattern (`theme.svelte.ts`: plain localStorage, validate-on-load, fallback to device default) — NOT the `tabiya.assistance.v1.*` version-wrapper precedent; a two-field `{themeId, mode}` cannot have a migration problem worth machinery. Same lesson as [[validation-by-use-not-ceremony]]: process weight must track what can actually go wrong | ⚖️ ruled — routed to the in-flight theming cross-review |
| D976 ⚖️ | **OWNER RULING 2026-08-22 (theming, two answers): default = FOLLOW DEVICE SETTING with manual override; identity = a CATALOG of known color schemes, not one bespoke palette** — verbatim: *"we might as well give it a known color scheme? personally i like tokyo night linux a lot. but we might as well provide multiple themes... just like how ~/frameworks/monorepo the player and the webapp have a set of themes? ~/frameworks/mistserver also has it in the LSP there..."* Consequences: the theming RFC ships a theme catalog — Tokyo Night as the owner's named favorite, the existing warm-paper light retained as a theme, the FullDark warm-dark as a candidate — with the set-of-themes pattern **inherited from the owner's own reference repos** (`~/frameworks/monorepo` player+webapp themes, `~/frameworks/mistserver` LSP themes), read before drafting rather than reinvented. `prefers-color-scheme` picks the default light/dark member; the picker overrides per device. The compiler, cycle/widening checks and runtime semantic-event seal all still read only `derivation.inputs`. Implement the RFC's closed, non-empty, duplicate-free alternative conjunctions; validate every member independently; seal the selected member; retain existing conjunction bytes. This is also prerequisite infrastructure for semantic attraction's check/capture alternatives. | ✅ closed 2026-08-22 — compiler/runtime seal and positive/negative fixtures landed |

branch-scoring polish become the main work. Canonical matrix:

## Foundation primitives (✅ ALL THREE IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12)

**Status: complete.** F1 shipped as `rfc/archive/authored-explanation-surface.md`;
F3 then F2 shipped in that order as migrations 2 and 3. Defects D1, D2 and D3
closed with them. The table below is kept because the *finding* — that the work
missing across eight program items reduced to three primitives — is what made
the sequencing possible, and because later RFCs cite these names.

Note for anyone citing this section: `feedbackIsRevealed` no longer exists. F2
replaced it with `feedbackDisclosed` (`packages/runtime/src/feedback.ts:3`).
Coordinates below are pre-implementation and are historical.

Six parallel code-verified passes (`planning/breadth/`) found that the missing
work across all eight program items reduces to **three absent primitives**, each
blocking areas that never talk to each other, each small in isolation, and all
three mutually independent. Full evidence: `planning/breadth/synthesis.md` §2.

| Primitive | What is absent | Blocks |
|---|---|---|
| **F1 — per-scope reveal** | `feedbackIsRevealed(pack, run)` (`feedback-policy.ts:11`) is one boolean per run; reaching Pack A's first of three checkpoints would release prose for all three | B4 authored-prose delivery (the named prerequisite in the *implemented* `rfc/archive/authored-feedback-delivery.md`); the streamer overlay, which needs per-viewer withholding; coach-reveals-prose in academy sessions |
| **F2 — pack-optional run identity** | A pack is mandatory at six layers; the pack-blind branch at `service.ts:145-152` is reachable only from tests, and the browser's `CreateRunRequest` cannot express a pack-less start | Just Play and from-position starts (#3), Arena leg import (#8), the pack playtest harness (#6). Must land together with D2 |
| **F3 — a subject** | `grep -riE "learnerId\|userId\|profileId\|accountId"` over all source returns nothing; the only actor token is a browser-local UUID and there is one database table | all of B7; host/participant/spectator roles in B5; the fix for D1. One migration now versus three later |

**A companion finding worth keeping visible:** the foundation RFCs cut slots that
no surface ever filled — `outcome.reached`, `transfer.scheduled`,
`human_model_predicted`, `feedback.generated`, `CheckpointInteraction.prediction`,
the drill-address grammar, and the generic predicate evaluator are all shipped,
tested, and have **zero producers**. Breadth-first worked: the contracts exist
and what remains is mostly producers and surfaces. The mirror risk is that a
slot with no producer reads exactly like a working feature — which is how five
RFC drafts died, and why every row in this pass carries a `file.ts:line`.

## Open defects (🐞 — found by the alignment pass, not yet fixed)

**Ledger id assignment — instituted 2026-08-15, AMENDED 2026-08-16 after it failed once.** Ids
here are assigned by *reading this file*, so a row committed between an agent-s read and its
write collides silently — it happened twice on 2026-08-15 (renumbered to D117 and D121–D127).
The fix was disjoint id blocks per parallel agent. **That fix then failed on its own third
run:** blocks were issued *in briefs* and never written here, so codex — correctly told to take
*"the next free id above the highest issued block"* — took **D203**, which was a
cross-reviewer-s, because it could not see a block that existed only in another agent-s prompt.
Renumbered to D233. **The hole was the convention-s, not codex-s.**

**Amended rule: a block is registered HERE when it is issued, not when its rows land.** The
table below is the register. An agent may use only its own block; anyone without one takes the
next free id above the highest registered block.
| Block | Finding / obligation | Disposition / history (not status) |
|---|---|---|

Weakened engines sample eval-noise uniformly, which reads as drunk, not weak. **Our own measurements bound the problem**: raw Maia banding buys 29–40 real Elo per 100 band points below learner resolution ([[D335]]/[[D336]]); Maia converts only **88.1–91.9% of won endgames** (`maia-endgame-fidelity`), so human-likeness needs an engine floor in simple endings; Maia has no search, so it never "calculates" even where every human would. | D366 ✅ | **Our most-used endgame opponent is the one instrument never measured in endgames.** Owner 2026-08-16: *"isn't that THE place where humans play so different from agent?"* Measured on the corpus: **12 of 14 endgame packs declare `human_common`** (Maia) and 2 declare `perfect_tablebase`. **Every instrument we own is mismatched exactly here.** (a) `perfect_tablebase` orders winning moves by **shortest DTZ** — distance-to-*zeroing* — so it provably beelines for the next capture or pawn move; "simplifies happily" is a property of the shipped code, and no human plays that way. (b) The explorer has **no endgame coverage at all** — R9 measured usable data ending at ply ~20 and zero by ply 27, while endgames begin far later. (c) **Maia is a policy network with no search**, which is precisely the regime where search matters most and a policy head is weakest — and it is our default. **The product question the owner's framing exposes:** a human-like endgame opponent is simultaneously the **most valuable** thing we could have (it is where technique gaps actually decide games) and the **least verified** thing we ship. The measurable form is not "is Maia strong" but *"is Maia wrong the way a human at that band is wrong"* — plausible technique failures — **or wrong arbitrarily**, which is noise wearing a human's name. The tablebase gives exact ground truth for result-preservation at ≤7 pieces, so this is answerable | ✅ **ANSWERED 2026-08-16, `design/research/maia-endgame-fidelity.md`** — 1,095 probes, 0 errors, 507 tablebase-probed positions from 11 of the 14 endgame packs, at the **0.7/0.9** temperature those packs actually declare rather than the code default. **Human-shaped, decisively:** the 84 errors live on **6 of 45 positions and 5 distinct moves**, modal error share **0.95–1.00** against **0.58–0.64** if the erring move were uniform over the same dropping moves. **All 84 are `win→draw`; zero `win→loss`, zero `draw→loss`** — where a uniform-random legal move concedes the full point on 10.7% of winning and 27.6% of drawn roots. `argmax(policy)` preserves at the identical rate, so the errors are **the model's belief, not the sampler's tail** — lowering temperature would not remove them. **Band-calibrated not at all:** 88.1 / 88.9 / 91.9% at 1100 / 1500 / 1900, **43 of 45 positions tied** between the extremes (sign p=0.5), with band application verified per probe (810/810 sent `Elo` after the `SelfElo`/`OppoElo` defaults; 45/45 positions produced three distinct policy vectors, zero collisions). **So the mode is sound and the `targetElo` on those twelve packs is the unsupported claim** |

**Live collision, 2026-08-16: `D203` is used twice.** The `pack-graduation` cross-review was
issued the block **D203–D212** and may use no other id; while it was measuring, the selection-
integrity commits (`fc99ba1`/`5835dfc`) took **D203** as *"the next free id above the highest
issued block"* — which it was not, because this block had been issued in a brief but not yet
registered on this line. Both rows are below. **The convention has a hole and it is this one:
"the highest issued block" is only knowable from a file that the issuing brief does not write
to.** Resolution is the owner's: renumber the selection-integrity row to **D233** (the first id
above the highest block now registered), or renumber this cross-review's first row. Fix for the
hole: a block is registered **on this line the moment it is issued**, not when its rows land.

| D148 🐞 | **The D126 ruling does not reach a single `cost: unmeasurable`, and the reason is the schema, not the corpus.** `$defs/deviationCost` admits exactly three shapes — `cp` (basis `engine` or `material`), `mate` (basis `engine` or `tablebase`) and `unmeasurable` — so there is no corpus-basis cost, and a result split cannot be written into the field at all. The semantic block is stronger than the structural one: *cost* is a quality claim by definition, so converting a split into one is precisely the conversion the ruling refuses. Measured at `a7e700d`: `commitMove` pushes `move.committed` and `outcome.reached` **in one `appendEvents` drafts array** (`runtime.ts:346-351`), `reachCheckpoint` emits its checkpoint then its segment in two back-to-back calls (`:454`, `:461-473`), and `commitMove` deliberately emits any `branch.forked` *before* the opponent selection (`:298-322`) — so all three gaps are empty by construction and **no existing event type is tolerated in any of them**. (2) The real hazard is subtler and is not written down anywhere: the three gaps stay closed **only because every emitter happens to bracket them inside one synchronous call**, a property no test asserts, no type enforces and any future `await` between two `appendEvents` calls silently breaks. A user-gesture-timed event would make that accidental bracketing load-bearing forever, and its failure mode is a `TypeError` surfacing as a 500 that discards the learner's gesture. Also weakening the read-time framing: `RunStorage` serves a live run from `#snapshots` without replaying, and `listRuns` reads `summary_json` only | ✅ closed by the runtime-invariant batch — one real checkmating run now exercises and pins selection→commit, checkpoint→segment, and commit→outcome adjacency |

Board annotation is the first case (one line — *"the voice should acknowledge what the learner circled"* — would put learner-chosen squares into the allowlist and let the model say `e5` about a position where nothing validated mentions `e5`), and a byte-identity test over the un-plumbed state cannot detect it | 🐞 open, found 2026-08-16 by the `board-annotation` cross-review |
| D215 🐞 | **`Cursor.branchId` is history-dependent, so any key built from it is a function of the visit rather than of the tree.** `rewind` (`packages/runtime/src/runtime.ts:398-400`) selects `isAncestor(run, nodeId, run.activeCursor.nodeId) ? run.activeCursor.branchId : target.branchId` — rewinding to an **ancestor** keeps the current branch id; rewinding anywhere else adopts the target node's. `Node.branchId` is fixed per node and `Cursor.branchId` is not, so the same node in the same tree presents different `(branchId, nodeId)` pairs on different visits: fork from N to B′, then rewind to N, and the cursor reads `B′:N`, not `B:N`, until a rewind lands off the current path. Nothing is wrong with `rewind` — the behaviour is what makes "the fork clears the board" work at the fork node itself, which `Node.branchId` could not deliver — but it means **branch-keyed persistence is conditionally invisible**, and no existing consumer had noticed because nothing else persists against the cursor's branch id. Recorded for every future feature keyed on "the line I am on" | 🐞 open, found 2026-08-16 by the `board-annotation` cross-review |

| D219 ✅ | **A skipped migration number is a one-way door, not a gap waiting to be filled.** The migration loop is `for (const migration of migrations) { if (migration.version <= version) continue; … }` (`apps/server/src/storage.ts:2197-2199`). The forward direction is fine — applying 23 to a database at 21 runs cleanly and sets `user_version = 23` — and it is the half that gets checked. The reverse direction is fatal and is the half that does not: **a database that has reached 23 will skip a later-landing 22 forever**, silently, with no error at open (`#migrate` throws only on `version > STORAGE_VERSION`, the opposite direction). So a draft that claims a number past an unlanded sibling's does not defer the sibling — it strands the sibling's tables on every existing database while fresh ones get them, which is worse than a collision because a collision is loud. The register's own practice already refuses holes and every one of its 22 rows is contiguous: migration 16 was *"rebased from an initial 15 claim"* and 21/22 were **reassigned to each other on 2026-08-16** at a cost its own row calls *"nothing but text"*. **Rule: a draft claims the next contiguous number at implementation time and reassigns a blocked sibling upward; it never leaves a hole.** Cheap guard: assert the migration array's versions are exactly `1..STORAGE_VERSION` | ✅ closed by the runtime-invariant batch — storage startup refuses any migration list other than the exact ordered range 1..STORAGE_VERSION, with missing, duplicate and reordered regressions |
| D247 🐞 | **`combinedRun` preserves exactly one identity across the pack-export boundary — the move path — so any key that must survive it is keyed on the UCI sequence, never on ids.** The remedy half of [[D217]], measured at `7650d41`. `exportPackRunPgn` ends `exportPgn(combinedRun(pack, run, branchIds))`; `combinedRun` reduces the authored spine and the played branches to `CombinedPath.moves` (bare UCI arrays), dedupes them by their joined UCI string in `uniquePaths`, and replays them through `createRun` + `commitMove`, forking at `sharedPrefix` — which itself locates a node by walking children whose `moveUci` matches. Node ids, branch ids, seqs and cursors are all regenerated; **the root-relative UCI path is preserved exactly and is unique within a tree**, so it is the only usable address. Two consequences nothing else records: `uniquePaths` collapses two branches with identical move sequences into one, so a remap is many-to-one and must dedupe; and the combined tree contains **authored nodes the run never reached**, so anything keyed on `transposeKey` can surface at a position the run never visited. First applied by `rfc/archive/board-annotation.md` §3.1 | 🐞 open, found 2026-08-16 by the `board-annotation` author round |
| D248 🐞 | **A guard test that runs below the layer its barrier is breached at cannot fail, and a guard never shown to go red is not evidence.** Both halves are demonstrated inside one RFC. (1) `board-annotation`'s criterion 2 asserts byte-identical `evidencePacket` output with and without marks — but the hazard it is cited against is a **`rest.ts` sentence splice**, which sits *above* `evidencePacket` and outside everything the criterion calls, so the test is sound and structurally blind. (2) Its proposed replacement grepped six pinned line numbers, four of which name assembly sites and two splice sites, while the natural violation is a **seventh** splice line the enumeration cannot see — and the numbers had drifted within a day. **Rule: a barrier criterion runs at the layer the barrier can be breached at, is matched by pattern rather than by line, and carries a positive control proving the assertion can report a planted violation.** Cheap, and it is the difference between a guard and a decoration | 🐞 open, found 2026-08-16 by the `board-annotation` author round |

So the owner-s proposal has **no mechanism whatsoever** today, and the honest first question is not *how do we build a clock* but *what is the smallest thing that produces the felt pressure* — a countdown that ends the encounter, or a soft budget that changes what assistance can be consumed. | D331 💡 | **Time is a difficulty axis that constrains the learner WITHOUT touching the power curve — and it may be the missing lever.** `design/06` §5 rules that **what escalates is LEGIBILITY, not power**, and that the power curve is flat by construction. Every difficulty lever found so far is therefore either opponent band (measured, `[1000,2400]`), decidability tier, encounter horizon, or capability suppression. **A clock is a fifth, and it is different in kind: it constrains the learner-s own computation rather than adding or removing anything the product gives them.** It also interlocks with the coaching-versus-cheating criterion landed 2026-08-16 (*distance from the answer*): **a hint you do not have time to read is not a hint**, so time pressure degrades assistance value continuously without any of it being withheld — which is exactly the *"balance cheating to win VS coaching to win"* problem the owner posed, solved by a mechanism that touches neither honesty policy nor inventory. It is also the first candidate that makes *"you-d need proper 2000 Elo skills"* a claim about the **learner** rather than about the encounter-s configuration, which the coaching dossier established the product otherwise cannot make. **Speculative and unmeasured — recorded as the reason D330 is worth more than a missing field** **REFUTED 2026-08-16, and in the direction that matters — this row-s central claim was claude-s and it was wrong.** The interlock hypothesis was *"a hint you do not have time to read is not a hint"*, so time would degrade assistance value continuously and preferentially suppress items nearest the answer. Measured over **43,272 rendered items** from shipped renderers: distance class explains **η² = 0.201** of the variance in reading length, and **0.038** once the refused `move` class is excluded — while **which renderer printed it explains 0.984**. ρ(distance rank, words) is **−0.046**, the order of the ρ = −0.143 this repo already treats as no relationship. **And the sign is inverted at the end that matters: `move` is the CHEAPEST class the product could ever print** — median **1 word / 0.3 s** against `ranking`-s **63 / 15.9 s**. So a clock is a gradient *toward* the answer: under time pressure a learner reaches for the move precisely because it reads fastest, which makes time a **cheating amplifier** rather than the balance mechanism this row proposed. It would also make difficulty a function of copy length, incentivising the compression of evidence into verdicts. **What survives is the by-product, and it is worth more than the hypothesis was:** at a 10+0 budget of 15.0 s/move ≈ 60 words, **≈6.6 `fact` items or 0.94 `ranking` items fit** — the slot number D78 licensed and never supplied, arrived at independently and **with no clock existing**. `design/research/time-as-a-difficulty-lever.md` | 💡 open, found 2026-08-16 |

| D355 💡 | **A game clock is NOT the refused pursuit clock — the discriminator is whether the budget survives a rewind, and it is one field's altitude.** `design/06` §5 refuses *"a pursuit clock is a retry price by another name"*, and §2c's own decomposition says only **how often** you may retry conflicts with `00` §76's *"experimentation without cost"*. Tested: a **run-pooled** clock makes the *k*-th retry cost more than the first — it is a rewind budget with a real-valued counter and the refusal is exactly right. An **attempt-scoped** clock that resets at the fork prices *deliberation inside one attempt* and touches none of §2c's three separable ideas. **The shipped placeholder already picked the safe altitude** `[V]`: `clockState` is declared on **`Node`** (`packages/runtime/src/types.ts:111`, alongside `branchId` at `:107`; mirrored at `schemas/drill_run.schema.json:265`) and written only from `CommitMoveOptions.clockState` (`runtime.ts:57`, applied `:341`) — nodes are path- and branch-scoped, so a clock built on the reserved field **rewinds with the board automatically**, and the refused version needs a **new run-level field**. That makes the ruling checkable in a diff rather than in prose. Two counter-arguments given in the dossier: a resetting clock has no teeth unless flag-fall rides `06` §5's *submitted-branch* verb (it can, and needs no new refusal class); and `06` §5's power/legibility dichotomy has **no slot** for a device that shrinks the learner's own capacity. `design/research/time-as-a-difficulty-lever.md` §2 | 💡 open, answered 2026-08-16, owner ruling pending — see [[D364]] |
| D356 💡 | **Reading cost does NOT track distance to the answer — the interlock hypothesis is refuted, and the number is not close.** D331 proposed that time pressure would degrade assistance *preferentially near the answer*, solving coaching-vs-cheating without touching honesty policy or inventory. Measured over **43,272 rendered items** from the shipped renderers (47 packs / 721 transitions / 609 positions, 25 shape entries, 43 real cached explorer responses, 105 recorded Maia candidate counts) `[V]`: variance in log(words) explained by **distance class** is **η² = 0.201** over four classes and **0.038** over the three the product may ship, while variance explained by **which renderer printed it** is **η² = 0.984**. Spearman ρ(distance rank, words) = **−0.046** over all items, **+0.125** excluding `move` — the same order as the ρ = −0.143 this repo already treats as *no relationship*. **Reading cost is a property of renderer verbosity, not of distance from the answer.** The within-class spread swamps the between-class difference: `kind` runs **6 words** (phase reading) to **298** (full shape panel) — a **50×** range; `ranking` runs **12** (the `human_divergence` marker) to **230** (the corpus page) — **19×**. So a clock would make an encounter's difficulty a function of **copy length**, and its standing incentive would be to compress evidence into verdicts — a move *down* the distance axis, i.e. toward the eval-bar trainer `00-thesis.md` exists to replace. The one point for the other side, stated: excluding `move`, the class medians do order correctly (6 < 9 < 63) — but η² = 0.038, and the effect is carried almost entirely by **one family**, the corpus page | 💡 open, measured 2026-08-16, `time-as-a-difficulty-lever.md` §3, `tools/d355-reading-cost-harness/` |

Inside one 10+0 move budget (15 s) a learner can read the answer **50 times over**, or **0.94** of one human-model split. Under time pressure the rational learner reads the shortest item that resolves the most of the live decision — which is precisely the item `coaching-versus-cheating-and-the-band-curve.md` calls cheating. **This interlocks directly with that dossier's open owner question:** under its option (a) `move` stays refused and a clock weakly favours the honest end (weakly — η² = 0.038); under option (c) `move` becomes purchasable pre-commit and **a clock becomes a cheating amplifier**. So the clock ruling should not be taken before the hint-ladder ruling | 💡 open, found 2026-08-16, blocks on the D317–D326 owner question |

| D332 🏗 | **Measure the learner-s Elo — the owner-s answer 2026-08-16, and it is LAW-8-LEGAL, which nobody had noticed.** Offered three denominators for progression (own-history histogram / catalogue / cadence) the owner declined the fork: *"we need history of learner too… and maybe catalogue progress… but the idea is again: go from elo 1000-2000 so maybe we need to just measure player ELO properly."* **The apparent collision dissolves on inspection.** `design/research/coaching-versus-cheating-and-the-band-curve.md` established the product can say neither *"played well"* nor *"run succeeded"* — no learner number exists anywhere, prediction grading was deleted at schema 0.8→0.9, and law 8 forbids grading moves. **But an Elo is not a claim about a move.** It is arithmetic over win/loss/draw against a known-strength opponent — structurally the same object as the explorer result splits the owner ruled admissible as `corpus_observed` (rung 4) on 2026-08-15: it says *what happened*, never *what is good*. **So Elo is the one learner measurement that requires grading nothing**, and it is the denominator the campaign has been missing since the power curve was ruled flat. It also makes *"you-d need proper 2000 Elo skills"* a claim about the **learner** rather than about the encounter-s configuration — the exact gap the coaching dossier identified and could not close. Its shape is simple and it is the one thing R10 did not do: play games, band against band, and count results | ✅ **ANSWERED 2026-08-16, `design/research/maia-band-outcome-transfer.md` — YES, and the units are the finding.** 16,660 whole games, 0 voids, paired-opening estimator with CIs clustered on the opening. **The band moves the result monotonically at every gap tested down to 100 points**, and D324's pre-registered ladder **passes** — all three adjacent CI pairs disjoint under both naive and cluster-robust intervals. | D340 🐞 | **Maia IS seeded — `--seed`, default 42 — and the shipped ENTRYPOINT passes none, so every sidecar this product has ever started ran at seed 42.** `maia3-uci` calls `seed_everything(cfg.seed)` before the engine is constructed (`/opt/maia3/maia3/uci.py:525`, `:68`; `utils.py:12-18` seeds `random`, NumPy and `torch.manual_seed`), and `workers/maia/Dockerfile`'s ENTRYPOINT is `maia3-uci --model 5m --use-uci-history` `[V]`. Measured, not inferred: two fresh containers given an identical 20-request sequence returned a **byte-identical** move sequence; a third at `--seed 7` returned a different one, itself reproducible; inside one process the same request repeated 20 times still returns 4 distinct moves `[V]`. **Both are true — the stream is stochastic per REQUEST and deterministic per PROCESS.** This corrects a reading, not a measurement: R5 (`maia-policy-scalar-stability.md` §9b) describes the mechanism exactly right, but its §10 concludes `human_common` is not reproducible and that flipping `seedHonored` *"would make the record less true"* — `seedHonored: false` is correct about the **UCI surface** and there is no UCI seed option, but the **process** is seed-honoring via a CLI flag, so `rfc/archive/resistance-spectrum.md` open question 1 has a determinism route nobody costed. Whether to pass `--seed` in the image, and whether the identity record should say so, is the RFC tier's call | 🐞 open, found 2026-08-16 |
| D341 🐞 | **An unseeded parallel engine-vs-engine harness manufactures duplicate games, and the failure mode is a control that returns exactly the right answer.** The first run of the D333 harness used twelve workers with no explicit seed; over 1,222 games its same-band control returned **611 of 611** mirrored pairs with **byte-identical move lists**, a **50.8%** duplicate-game rate, and a paired score of **exactly 0.500000 with a standard error of exactly 0.0** `[V]`. Mechanism is [[D340]] plus an even worker count: workers *s* and *s+1* received mirrored schedules from the same seed 42 and stayed in lockstep. **The control did not fail to detect a difference — it reported a perfect, zero-variance null, which is the most confident possible wrong answer.** Fixed by a distinct `--seed` per worker and an ODD worker count so worker never lines up with colour; the final run has 16,013/16,660 distinct move lists and 133/8,330 identical mirrored pairs. **Standing rule for this repo's future engine-vs-engine work: seed each worker explicitly, count distinct move lists, and treat a zero-variance control as a defect rather than a result** | 🐞 open, found 2026-08-16 |

| D344 💡 | **[[D365]]'s Glicko update needs the MEASURED opponent scale, not the declared band, and the factor is 4.3.** D365 already says *"a Glicko update against an opponent whose declared rating does not predict its results produces a confidently wrong number faster than Elo would"*. That is now a number: the declared band over-predicts the result gap by about **2.5× at full material and 3.5× over the corpus** ([[D335]]). A rating system fed the band as the opponent's rating converges quickly to a rating that is wrong by construction and whose RD shrinks anyway, because RD narrows on *volume*, not on *validity* — the uncertainty term does not protect against a mis-specified opponent. | D365 💡 | **Rating systems already solve [[D332]], and the one property that matters here is UNCERTAINTY.** Owner extension 2026-08-16: *"we can think of other ways to gauge progression… make it configurable in the profile or when opponents win/lose against bots readjust… there must be measures for this."* There are, and they are standard: **Elo** (K-factor, no uncertainty term), **Glicko/Glicko-2** (Lichess-s own system — carries a **rating deviation** and a **volatility** alongside the number), **TrueSkill** (μ and σ). **Glicko-2 is the obvious candidate and the reason is not accuracy, it is honesty.** RD lets the system say *"1450 ± 180"* and, more importantly, lets it **refuse to say anything** until RD narrows — which is the same discipline as the tablebase abstaining outside range, the explorer abstaining below 100 games, and the `unmeasured` disposition. A product that refuses to manufacture chess truth should not manufacture a rating either, and every alternative here either asserts a bare number or has no term for its own ignorance. **The owner-s two mechanisms map exactly onto it**: *"configurable in the profile"* is a self-declared seed with a wide provisional RD (Lichess-s own onboarding), and *"readjust when they win/lose against bots"* is the update step. Neither needs invention. **Both are gated on [[D333]] in the same way** — a rating derived from games against Maia bands is only as meaningful as the bands are real, and a Glicko update against an opponent whose declared rating does not predict its results produces a confidently wrong number faster than Elo would. Note also the encoding fact from `design/research/maia-wdl-versus-human-outcome.md`: Maia already emits an expected score directly, `0.5 + cp/2000` exactly, which is the same quantity a rating system predicts — so there is a cross-check available that most implementations never get | 💡 open, owner extension 2026-08-16 |

## Authoring-format friction (💡 — raised by authors while writing real packs)

The point of authoring one pack per phase is to find these. Each is a concrete
proposal from someone who hit the limitation with content in hand, which is the
evidence the withdrawn contracts RFCs never had.

| Friction | Proposal | Raised by |
|---|---|---|
| A plan drill's objective cannot be expressed. Success is relative to the **captured intent** — did you execute the plan you committed to — but `successConditions` supports only intent-blind `reach_checkpoint`, so plan packs ship with no objective at all | Intent-relative success conditions. **Path found 2026-08-13 (`05` §5c): grade the plan by its structural consequence.** The predicate machinery ships and is authorable; only feature-level vocabulary (Q4b) is missing. Still connected to `intent_capture` being inert and to the objective-type widening in program #4 | Pack B (Carlsbad), 2026-08-12 |
| The on-ramp's blunder-guard knob has no encoding. `defect-sweep` removes `immediate_blunder_guard` from the schema because `feedbackPolicy` has no capability publication, no applied-policy record and no honest degradation — so `design/00-thesis.md`'s 1000–1400 lane loses one of the three knobs that define it. Re-add it as a *real* policy with those three properties, not as an enum value. **SHIPPED 2026-08-14 (`onramp-guard`): `immediate_guard` at pack 0.14, post-commit, two rung-0 tiers + recorded-eval tier. Scheduled note kept for history: v1 form is the post-commit guard — the move commits, the guard offers play-on-or-rewind — per the Dr. Wolf transformation (their pre-commit retract inverts commit-before-learning). Pre-commit form is invariant-review material if the owner's session says beginners need it** | 💡 raised by the defect sweep, 2026-08-13 |
| **For a middlegame pack the two authoring rules fight each other, and no instrument sees the fight.** "Follow the most-played move at the band" is what makes a spine corpus-grounded; "the referenced shape must keep firing" is what makes it a *structure* pack. Measured 2026-08-15: from the French Advance family root the most-played walk liquidates the d4 pawn and `closed-centre-chain` stops firing within three plies; the Grünfeld's most-played reply is a central lever that ends the fianchetto race; the Maroczy's most-played line survives intact. Authors resolved it by hand, one extra walk at a time (~12 min each), and each stated the departure in a SPINE SELECTION RULE provenance line. A walker that reports, per node, whether a named expression still holds after each candidate move would make the conflict visible instead of archaeological | Middlegame wave (10 packs), 2026-08-15 |
| Deviations have no link to a plan class. 11.a3 and 11.Rab1 are literally the *same plan*, and `accepted_alternative` says nothing about that | Optional `planClassId` on a deviation | Pack B, 2026-08-12 |
| `concept_violation` does two different jobs — a **timing** error (right plan, wrong moment) and a **plan-coherence** error (a move that contradicts the committed plan). Collapsing them loses the distinction the feedback most needs to make | ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-08-15 by `deviation-classes`.** Optional multi-valued `mistake` separates `plan`, `timing`, and `tactical` from the unchanged objective-relative class; no machine reclassifies the author's judgment. | Pack B, 2026-08-12 |

| Comparison column ceiling | 💡 **owner ruling wanted.** `n-way-comparison.md` caps a comparison set at 8 branches and originally cited `design/03-product-breadth.md:288` for it — **that citation was fabricated; no such statement exists** (the only "eight" there is eight program items). The RFC now asserts 8 on its own grounds. Design should either ratify the number or set its own, because it is a product constraint on the surface the whole rewind-and-compare loop leans on | `03-product-breadth.md`, Q9 |
| Prediction distribution delivery | 💡 the withholding barrier **truncates** the event stream at the first engine-feedback event, so a synchronous response is a legitimate and distinct delivery path. Worth stating in design, since "it isn't gated" and "it is delivered" were conflated once already | `explanation-grounds`, ADR-0006 |

## In-run assistance surfaces (💡 batch, owner ideas 2026-08-13)

Three ideas from the owner, ledgered on utterance. They compose: (1) says *what
kind of position this is*, (2) says *what evidence applies to that kind*, and (3)
is a distinct thing — deterministic sight, not evidence at all.

**Design home: `05-in-run-experience.md`**, written the same day so these do not
sit as loose candidates. All three are generic in-run features — true whether or
not a pack is loaded — and that document places them: the classifier is what
makes the assistance rail selectable (§4), configuration per session context is
one of its four varying axes (§4), and discovered-threat sight is **rung 0** of
the assistance ladder (§3), the only rung that cannot manufacture chess truth.

| Idea | Take | Home |
|---|---|---|
| **Phase classifier with an in-run sidebar** | Early/middle/endgame surfaced live during play, not just as a catalogue filter. Partly covered already: Q4c owns automatic recognition, D6 is `phase` never reaching the client, and the Learn IA is organized on it — but all of that is *navigation*. A live in-run classifier is new, and it is what makes (2) selectable. Must stay non-authoritative over curated pack boundaries (standing rule) and must abstain honestly rather than guess | Q4c, D6, `03-product-breadth.md` |
| **Configurable engine/assistance sidebar** | Run simulations, ask for best move or a move *set*, from whichever source is applicable — Stockfish for evaluation, Maia for what humans at a level actually play, Lichess explorer for frequency, Syzygy where the material allows. **The new part is not the sources — B4 already owns those — it is that assistance becomes configurable per session context.** Just Play, streamer mode and a curated drill want different defaults, and "what assistance is available here" is currently implicit everywhere. Includes structural classifiers for middlegame ideas (the Dragon bishop wanting an open long diagonal), which is the deterministic-features work in Q4b rather than an engine question | B4, Q4b, Q8, `03-product-breadth.md` §Intelligence |
| **Discovered-threat visualisation ("shift to see two moves of consequence")** | 💡 **transition arithmetic shipped 2026-08-15; the visual/hypothetical surface remains open.** `transition-primitives` now answers “what changed on the committed move?” on request with rules-derived attack, defence, line, flight-square, duty and irreversibility facts. R3 refused an unasked live tier. Holding a modifier over a candidate move or projecting two plies remains a distinct anti-contamination/form decision and is not claimed by that RFC. | ADR-0005, ADR-0006, opponent-intent row, Q4b, Q9, `transition-primitives` |

## Strategic reading and pivotal detection (💡 batch, owner 2026-08-13)

Specified in `05-in-run-experience.md` §5/§5a/§5b; rows kept so none is lost.

| Idea | Take | Home |
|---|---|---|
| **Prophylaxis / denial as a first-class readable** | "After a4, Black's knight can never use b5 again" is rules arithmetic — rung 0, cannot be wrong. A denial move is **invisible to every eval-first tool** because nothing happened, which makes it the clearest demonstration that rung 0 sees things an evaluation cannot explain. Mirror of the ledgered opponent-intent prompt | `05` §5, ADR-0005 |
| **Structural readables: outposts, diagonals, pressure balance** | All three are computable without an engine — an outpost is a pawn-defended square in enemy territory unattackable by enemy pawns; a diagonal's blockers can be named; attackers and defenders can be counted. **Detection is free; significance is rungs 2–5 and must be attributed.** Q4b's deterministic-feature work is this | `05` §5, Q4b |
| **Tactical build-up ("what is each side aiming at")** | The one part of the owner's list that is *not* deterministic. Rung 2/3 territory, and the place where a strategic classifier would be tempted to manufacture truth. Keep separate from the structural readables above rather than bundling them into one "threat classifier" | `05` §5, ADR-0005, Q8 |
| **Auto-detected pivotal moments for pack-less play** | The gem, per the thesis amendment. Honest detectors: irreversibility (rung 0), phase change, **human divergence** — the Maia distribution at the learner's level splitting several ways, which is a fact about the distribution rather than a claim about chess and uses a model already shipped — and option collapse. Engine eval swing is deliberately *excluded* as a primary detector: it finds where someone erred, which is the post-mortem framing this product replaces, and it cannot fire before the error | `05` §5a, Q4c, B2 |
| **Content transfer test** | 📐 owner test 2026-08-13, audited in `04` §0a: *does authoring this make Just Play better?* Result for the shipped format — **no**. Every field is anchored to the pack's own move tree except four, and the three that carry reusable knowledge cannot escape: `planClasses` are inlined per pack, `concepts` have no cross-pack identity, `feedbackClaims` have no trigger so they can never fire. Authoring a pack today improves exactly one drill and contributes nothing to an unauthored game. **Rule: content earns its cost by how much of it fires in a game nobody authored** — not a ban on line content (opening theory *is* a move sequence) but a budget and a direction, and the reusable half currently rounds to zero. Minimal fix: packs **reference** shape entries instead of inlining them; `fenPredicate`/`materialBalance` are already the two shipped triggers that key on the position rather than the tree, so the machinery exists and the authoring habit does not | `04` §0/§0a, B11, Q4b |
| **Feature-level structural predicates (the unification)** | ✅ The shared structural-expression grammar is executable in pack objectives and shape entries. Predicate waves 1–3 supply eighteen detector kinds, and `plan_consequence` now binds an authored plan class to its reusable shape-plan success signature without claiming intent. Pack B exercises the binding on its authored line. | `05` §5c, Q4b, `predicate-wave-3` |
| **Game story — a finished game as ~8 pivotal slides** | ✅ **SHIPPED — verified 2026-08-15**, `docs/game-import-and-story.md` §Grounded moments: `GET /runs/:id/story` is a disclosure-gated derived projection over shipped deterministic detectors (irreversible moves, phase changes, option collapse, eval pivots, first endgame entry, shape spans); the payload returns all moments with a deterministic rank and **the client displays up to eight**, ordered by ply. Voice may phrase the packet, never add chess claims. Was carried as open in claude's 2026-08-15 inventory — an error caught the same day by checking `docs/` instead of the ledger — original row: owner 2026-08-14: *"we have our pivotal moments... maybe we can summarize a game with states and how it influenced the game? a set of 8 slides."* **Everything it needs is the backward half of machinery we already specified or shipped**: retrospective pivotal detection (`05` §3a — eval swing is *permitted* backward, plus objective-state transitions and last-point-the-result-was-available), phase classification (B10, in flight), structural naming (B9, shipped), and the outcome grade. A slide = position + what kind of moment it was (detector-attributed) + what changed after it. **Post-game, so ADR-0006 does not bite** — the game is over, nothing left to contaminate; this is the one surface where the full ladder may speak at once. Natural tie-ins: the share/spectate links (a story is the shareable artifact a run link never was), session-to-pack distillation (a slide's moment is a candidate drill root), and Just Play's review path. Law-8 rule: each slide *names* its detector and evidence; the connective narrative is LLM-as-voice territory (packet-bound, §3b-i). Slide count is presentation, not contract | `05` §3a/§5a, B10, share links, teardown-taketaketake (research in flight) |
| **Own-game review — import one game into the rehearsal frame** | ✅ **SHIPPED — verified 2026-08-15**, `docs/game-import-and-story.md`: `imported` is a third session kind; one pasted PGN or one public lichess game URL (chess.com refused with guidance, no public per-game contract); selecting a story moment rewinds to its `entryNodeId` and creates a `story-reentry` branch, so the game opens back into live play rather than a report — which is exactly the line that keeps it out of the rejected v1 identity. **Export ships too** (all branches, rehearsal branches as legal PGN variations). Browser-tested end to end — original row: owner 2026-08-14: *"we said it's not a game review, but we have all the pieces (+the LLM) — in context of our rewind / classifiers."* **The v1 boundary, pinned:** what stays rejected is mine-games→detect-weaknesses→generate-lessons as identity and mandatory entry (AGENTS.md, ADR-0003). What this is: **one game, imported by choice, as an entry context** — backward pivotal detection finds the moments (`05` §3a), game-story renders them as slides, tapping a slide rewinds *there*, branch, replay vs human-like resistance with structural reading on. The review IS the rehearsal entry — the anti-version of the engine-review screen, not a return to it. **Shipped pieces:** PGN export w/ variations (B3), Arena leg PGN import on a request path (live-sessions — verify reusability as the parser seam), backward detectors (B10), structural naming (B9), position runs (F2 + B11's player). **Missing:** a first-class import endpoint creating an imported run from PGN or a lichess/chess.com game URL (external fetch = ToS/licence note needed), and the review surface itself. Composes with game-story into one RFC — both consume B10's backward detection. Account-level fetch-all-my-games stays out | `05` §3a, game-story row, ADR-0003, B2 entry contexts |
| **Recurring sharp edge: rewind cancels pending evidence** | 📐 pattern note, 2026-08-14. `onRewound` (`apps/server/src/evidence-queue.ts:148-169`) cancels queued jobs and drops staged results for off-path nodes — correct for live play (a pruned line's evidence is moot) but **two independent drafts designed around it in one day**: branch-groups (lockstep rotation's rewind cancels sibling jobs mid-round) and game-import (a slide tap IS a rewind, and mid-batch would destroy later slides' evals). Both solved it locally (recovery via `/analysis` + honest absence; a `ready` gate). If a third consumer hits it, the fix is structural: evidence jobs for *historical/batch* analysis should not ride the live-play queue's pruning rules — a batch class exempt from `onRewound` | evidence-queue, branch-groups §, game-import § |
| **Opening-wave authoring frictions (2026-08-14)** | 💡 batch from the six-pack wave: ✅ candidate identities key by learner side; ✅ first-move alternatives use `atStart`; ✅ `predicate-wave-3` distinguishes present from prospective shape references and publishes uncheckable plan consequences; still open: the missing post-dxc5 residue shape. | `planning/content-era/log.md` 2026-08-14, shape library, pack schema |

| **The engine request contract (promote to design tier)** | 💡 named 2026-08-15 by `rfc/engine-request-contract.md`, and it is the sibling of the declared-vs-executable law rather than an instance of it: **that law governs what a document may SAY; this one governs what a call must DO.** *An engine request must close over the instrument state its answer depends on* — **state** (every option whose value changes the answer is sent by that request, never inherited), **clear** (every accumulated search state the request does not want is cleared), **bind** (the clear and the search it protects are ONE queued exchange — independently violable, and the `position-seeds` reset is a pure *bind* failure with correct clearing), **bound** (every value sent lies inside a published range, or the request is refused by name), **record** (every value applied and the answer taken appear in the persisted record). Its one-line form: ***state a request does not state is state the previous request chose.*** Four ledgered defects are each exactly one missing obligation — D35 is *clear*, D58 is *state* + *record*, D59 is *state* + *record* (the RFC's own preferred remedy widens the window, which is *state*; the original *record*-only mapping was retrofitted), D60 is *bound* — and the two laws overlap on **two obligations** (*bound* wholly, *record* partly) at **one ledger row**, D60 — the draft's "exactly one point" was contradicted two sentences later by its own text — which is why that row cites the older law correctly and is silent on the other three. Belongs in design tier once the RFC lands | declared-vs-executable law, `engine-request-contract` |

Path branching is thematically chess-native (the aggressive route vs the solid route); relics/card-unlocks = encounter-unlocked shape entries (row above); a lost fight is not game-over — it becomes a **save node** (recovery-as-skill as level design). Map generation can be seeded from tracks (`04` §1) + priority data. No skill numbers needed anywhere — advancement is event facts. **RULED 2026-08-14: the map gates its own rewards, the library stays open** — a chosen mode over an always-open catalog | `04` §1 Track, encounters row, outcome grading, trajectories |

| **Multi-branch view shapes (tree / carousel / stack / grid / fractal subdivision)** | 💡 owner 2026-08-13. **The view follows the shape being examined, and there are three** — a *run over time* (sequential forks; the interesting relation is ancestry, so a thread or tree), a *group at one moment* (N parallel candidates; the relation is sibling difference, so a grid), and a *single branch deep* (one board plus timeline). Treating those as one problem is why "which view" feels unanswerable. The owner's **fractal subdivision** — a rectangle that splits on each fork — fits the second shape well and the first poorly, since it shows containment rather than sequence. **Correction 2026-08-13:** an earlier version of this row computed a "depth budget" from how many boards fit legibly in a fixed viewport (27 at 200px, 81 unreadable at 114px) and called it a ceiling. **That was the wrong question** — the owner pointed out pan/zoom removes it, and they are right: a canvas can hold an arbitrarily deep grid and you navigate it. What actually survives is not a pixel limit but an **overview-versus-detail tradeoff**: at any zoom you can see the whole structure or read a board, not both. The answer to that is **semantic zoom** — cells render *different content* by scale, not the same content smaller: at far zoom a cell shows result, structure name and objective state; at near zoom it shows the board. A pan/zoom canvas inside a region is also compatible with the viewport-contained shell, since it is not document scroll. Also interacts with: the walkthrough finding that compare *selection* is cumbersome (a branch group makes selection disappear — the group **is** the selection), and the branch-race row as the two-board special case | Q9, `03` §Branch groups, comparison-column-ceiling row |
| **Branch ranking for pruning** | 💡 owner 2026-08-13: *"we need good UX on ranking all the branches… rank with Stockfish right? we need to prune and drop stupid branches."* **The need is real and the engine is the wrong ranker.** Three reasons. (1) Ranking branches by evaluation *is* "an engine review screen with a rewind button" — the failure shape `AGENTS.md` names as the thing this product must not become. (2) It breaks ADR-0006 on the comparison surface: telling a learner branch B is worse **before they have played it out** hands them the answer, which is the same contamination the whole withholding barrier exists to prevent. (3) It is usually answering the wrong question — *"stupid branch"* in practice means *"I abandoned it after two moves"*, not *"the engine dislikes it"*. **Rank for attention, not for quality.** The signals that decide which branches deserve screen space are already computed and are all rung 0 — `branchCards` (`apps/web/src/lib/screen-model.ts:135-152`) carries `objectiveState`, `terminal`, `intent`, `firstMove`, `forkNodeId`, `origin`; add depth, and structural divergence from siblings (a branch that transposed back teaches nothing a sibling does not). A branch you committed an intent to and played to a terminal outweighs a two-ply stub, and no evaluation was consulted. **Engine evaluation is legitimate as one column in review, after the outcome — never as the sort key.** And **prune must mean collapse, never delete**: *an attempt is never destroyed* is an invariant (`05` §1), because the product's one original claim is comparison of two preserved attempts. Note the tension to keep straight: `rfc/archive/n-way-comparison.md` normatively forbids ranking fields and comparative sentences — that prohibition is about *asserting chess quality*, and ordering a rail by completeness and divergence does not assert any | Q9, `05` §1/§3, ADR-0006, `rfc/archive/n-way-comparison.md` |
| **Silence as the assistance default** | 📐owner 2026-08-13, and it corrects a default `05` §3 got wrong: rung 0 being the *safest* thing to show is not an argument for it being **on**. Proactive assistance is in tension with the thesis — telling a learner their knight has no outpost before they move coaches them past the mistake that would have taught them. Default during committed play is **silence**; the rail exists and the learner may open it. `05` §3a | `05` §3a, ADR-0006, `00-thesis.md` |
| **Guided ("clippy") mode** | 📐owner 2026-08-13. Live tips while you play — and it is **not** an exception to the silence default but the **shape library rendered live**, i.e. what B9+B10+B11 produce with assistance turned up. **One line carries the design: a tip may name what *kind* of position this is and what that kind is generally about; it may not say what is good *here*.** "This is a Carlsbad; the standard plans are minority attack, central break, kingside" is shape content, true independent of this game. "Play the minority attack" is an evaluation, and during committed play that is the ADR-0006 violation. Not the Clippy people hated: rung-0/authored so it cannot be casually wrong, structure-keyed so it is not generic, delivered as the already-ruled **passive marker the player may open** rather than a modal, and it is a chosen mode. **Real risk, distinct from all of those: tips that never stop remove the need to look** — rung 0 exists to teach seeing, and naming the outpost every time does the seeing for the learner. So it is band-shaped: natural default for the 1000–1400 on-ramp where naming a concept precedes rehearsing it, off by default above, with an explicit intent that it fades | `05` §3b, B9/B10/B11, `00-thesis.md` §Target player |
| **LLM as the guided-mode voice** | 💡 owner 2026-08-13 (*"we don't have the LLM for nothing… the clippy can be beautifully annoying"*). Correct division and squarely inside ADR-0005, which forbids the LLM **inventing** chess truth and has never forbidden it having a voice: **the classifier is the source, the shape entry is the claim, the LLM is the mouth.** Contract is checkable — an evidence packet (detected structure, plan classes, rung-0 facts that fired, phase) is assembled first, the model gets the packet plus a persona and may choose wording/order/tone, and **may not introduce a chess noun, square, move or judgement absent from the packet**. `docs/explanation-grounds.md` already ships grounded rendering of this shape, so this extends a mechanism rather than inventing one. "Beautifully annoying" is a real property: personality makes a concept memorable, and what must be annoyed is the learner's *complacency*, not their play — hence the passive-marker delivery, opinionated inside a panel they opened, never seizing the board. **Cost/degradation under hosted multi-user:** per-move generation is a per-user bill and a per-ply latency budget, and is unnecessary — tips fire on detected shapes, which are sparse, and the shape entry already carries canonical authored prose. Default is the authored text with the LLM re-voicing on request; provider absent means the learner loses the personality and keeps the identical claim | `05` §3b-i, ADR-0005, B4, B10 |
| **Declared honest target as the motivator** | 💡 owner 2026-08-13, recorded at thesis level. Being worse feels like prolonging a defeat, which is why people bail out of exactly the endgames that teach most. Declaring the true target up front — *drawn with correct defence, hold it* — makes being worse the **premise** rather than the failure, and gives a winnable goal from a losing position. Binding constraint: **the target is only settable where the result is assessable** — tablebase below eight pieces, authored or engine judgement above and labelled as such. Declaring "this is held" wrongly is real damage: the learner grinds a defence of a position that was already lost | `00-thesis.md`, `01` §Outcome types, B9 |
| **Punishment-free experimentation** | 💡 owner 2026-08-13. Human-like resistance makes a game worth playing; preserved branches make trying something free — play the dubious sacrifice, see what a real opponent does, still have the position you left. **Guard rail:** the consequence stays mandatory and only the retry is free. *Rewind is an experiment, not an undo* (`05` §1) — frictionless rewind during play would mean nothing is ever committed and the rehearsal collapses. **Play it out, then go back; never take it back.** Also implies the rewind should be *offered* after a failed recovery, not merely available | `00-thesis.md`, `05` §1/§3a |
| **Recovery as a first-class skill** | 📐owner 2026-08-13: *"the fuck up, then recover, and if recovery fails grind out the draw."* That sequence is most of real chess at 1400–2000 and every trainer skips it because they all optimise for finding the best move. Vocabulary already exists — `01` §Outcome types has **save** = rescue a worse position — but it has been a drill variant rather than the normal path through a run. Adds a fourth thing a run can be about: not *what should I have played* but **what can I still do from here** | `05` §3a, `01` §Outcome types, B2 |
| **Retrospective pivotal detection** | 📐owner 2026-08-13 (*"or go back to that pivotal point"*). Resolves an apparent contradiction: `05` §5a excludes engine eval swing as a **live** detector because it finds where someone erred and cannot fire before the error — that stands. But *going back* is a backward-looking question, and there eval swing is exactly right. **Forward** (is a real decision arriving?) → irreversibility, phase change, Maia divergence, option collapse. **Backward** (where did it turn?) → eval swing, objective-state transitions, the last point the result was still available. Using the backward detector forward is the post-mortem framing this product replaces | `05` §3a, §5a |
| **Endgame steering as named technique** | Recognize the type, name the technique, let the learner execute, grade the result — never "play Rc8". Most tractable phase for honest guidance: types are structurally recognizable, techniques are finite and named, and ≤7 pieces has tablebase ground truth | `05` §5b, `04-content-architecture.md` §4 |

Inside a category-preserved endgame **|dtz| decreases under optimal play**, so `tablebase_dtz_regression` at `byAtLeast: 1` means *"you left the shortest conversion path"* — which **is** `bestmove`, the arm the rule refuses by name, reached through a scalar the same clause calls a measurement. **The general form, now the rule: the subject being a measurement is NOT sufficient — the threshold must sit off the instrument's optimality boundary.** Only `engine_eval_swing` demonstrably does (its shipped `minimum: 50` sits far off; the DTZ floor was 1). The **low** edge ≈800–1000 fails on *readability* — median listed mass falls to 0.833 at band 0, so **the contract fails before the model does**. **Methodology lesson worth keeping:** the definition claude proposed (*is the distribution distinguishable between adjacent bands?*) holds over the **entire** advertised range and fails **totally** outside it — it would have found nothing. The edges only appear under *ordering* and *readability*, neither of which claude thought to ask for | R10, engine request contract |

Any future "is this primitive informative" measurement must compare against alternatives, never against spine frequency alone, or it will systematically prefer the wrong instruments | R3, predicate waves |

Also B3 (catalogue identity used as instance identity — two searches with the same projection version produce identical refs, against 65.6% depth-8/12 first-move agreement), B5, B6 (a global *engine empty ⇒ off* would disable an available theory hint), B7 (no end-to-end path) and B8 | 🐞 open — redraft after the selector's exploration gate is met |

The repair is to **stop joining**: no signature change, no renderer-contract change, no provider-contract change. **The real cost is elsewhere and is worth the owner's eye**: byte-exact spans mean the model may utter a judgement word only by quoting the deterministic sentence *verbatim*, so it cannot paraphrase one — which invalidates `rfc/move-quality-grades.md` §6's mechanism claim that *"the LLM may re-voice 'mistake'"* (`:380-389`). Failing safe helps: `renderVoice` falls back to deterministic text (`guidance.ts:163-170`), so tightening can only raise the fallback rate, never emit unguarded prose — but that rate is **unmeasured** | 📊 measured 2026-08-23 — `planning/platform-alignment/d1409-word-guard-repair.md`; follow-up RFC owed against `rfc/archive/adaptive-guidance.md` |

Worse for the theory case, **`plan` is in none of the three lists** — verified, 0 occurrences in `voice.ts`, as are `initiative`, `compensation` and `pressure` — and no scoping rule can repair a word no list contains. **The sharpest finding is the escalation vector**: a grade *sentence* frees only its own word, but **`blunder` becomes free the moment any packet sentence names the closed class** — which `grade.ts:192-194`'s mate-tier text and any `inaccuracy \| mistake \| blunder` caption do automatically, on exactly the surface [[D1273]] ruled. | D1496 💡 | **THE EARNED REWIND IS NOT A BALANCE — THE INCOME EVENT IS THE INTERFACE, AND THE NUMBER IS ONLY ITS RECEIPT.** [[D945]] asked for rewinds that are earned without being punitive, and the mechanism is precise: **punitive is a function of attribution.** A resource feels punitive when its loss is attributed to the learner's **error** — but charges are spent by **a gesture the learner chooses** and income is **verdict-blind** in the shipped fold. So every string keeps attribution on the gesture, and three words defuse the whole currency schema: **win or lose**. Two rules beyond the obvious ones: **the balance lives on the map, not in the rail** — the RFC currently seats `⟲ N` in **the same seat `postcommit_nudge` uses**, and an economy counter in the coaching seat teaches that *the coach is metered*; a persistent counter is also disclosure at every moment **except** the one that matters, where *"Rewind and branch — spends 1 of your 3 earned"* does the work. And **the carry-forward balance quietly prices early experimentation**: one run-scoped pool plus non-increasing act grants means a rewind spent in Act I is unavailable at the Act III boss, **so the rational play is to experiment least where the product most wants it.** No document had stated that | 💡 open — `design/research/ux-campaign.md` §6 |

Six options are costed with none picked, including two nobody had proposed: **a continuous cost** (Puzzle Storm's *"an error costs what you had accumulated, not a life"* — but its natural currency is charges, which **breaks the verdict-blind income clause** the humane answer rests on), and **the intermediate node setting the boss's terms** (*"the boss decides the run; the node decides the terms on which you meet the boss"*). Option D — the run gets harder — is the only one that turns failure into content, and it is **punitive adaptivity that inverts [[D945]]'s purpose**; its mirror, where failure **lifts** suppression, is more defensible and nobody has proposed it. Four properties should hold whichever way it goes: losing never locks content, the ending offers the preserved run, the catalogue diff renders identically on a lost run, and **the possibility of ending is announced before the boss** | 📊 measured 2026-08-24 — feeds [[D1300]]; `design/research/ux-campaign.md` §7.5 |
